name: faults-long-real-node
description: The weekly long fault set under load (#554, #487 S16 and L4): a managed regtest qbitd pair ramped to the fake node's difficulty, two frontends with an async standby streaming through a link the harness can cut and the primary's WAL on a 1 GiB fuse2fs volume, 2,000 sessions at 200 shares/s over a 20k window with six external tips over a 45-minute warm-up, then a faults phase that injects every #554 fault one at a time with a 10 s baseline, a 30 s hold and a 20 s recovery window: the WAL volume filled until PostgreSQL stops and then freed, a 20 ms one-way database delay, a PostgreSQL at max_connections, a SETTLEMENT_LOCK holder with a tip minted halfway, SIGKILL of the frontend holding a found block the node accepted, SIGTERM of a frontend with a found block's offer in flight, a rolling restart, a 50% reconnect storm, both frontends restarted over a backlog of six found blocks, the primary lost after a 5 s replication cut with the standby promoted, the fenced planned switch, and a found block held across a failover, while the public API and every /metrics are scraped. Each fault is held to its #554 pass criteria. About 60 minutes of run: the warm-up, then about 11 minutes of faults.
